I'm interested in what the recovering player still has to risk, and what the edge-guarder can actually do about it.

A hought about toxicity I’ve honestly been wondering for a while why the game gives players so much leeway when it comes to being toxic. I’ve heard from quite a few people who eventually quit after years of playing and once loving the game, simply because the constant taunting, sarcastic laughing/crying, and thumbs-down emotes after every match made the experience so miserable that they decided other games were just more fun.

Brawlhalla used to have a massive playerbase, so did it really never occur to the devs that selling emotes specifically designed to annoy, taunt, or make other players feel bad might eventually drive people away? And then there was the irony of making players “agree” to new terms and conditions telling them to be decent and non-toxic in-game, while the game itself basically monetizes the exact behavior they’re supposedly trying to discourage.

This is absolutely not a rant or me being salty, because I genuinely love the game, and will continue to play. It’s just a thought I wanted to share.

How do you properly coordinate with your teammate in 2v2s? I've been playing 2v2s with my duo, and one thing we're struggling with is knowing when to help each other out. For example, if my teammate gets caught in a combo, I'll sometimes try to interrupt the enemy, but I end up getting caught myself. Other times, we both chase the same opponent and end up hitting each other. Another problem is that when one of us gets pressured or comboed, we'll sometimes both start moving toward the same side of the map, which makes it easy for the enemies to pressure and hit both of us. Should we be trying to spread out more and approach from different angles, or is there a better way to handle these situations? How do you decide when to help your teammate versus when to focus on your own fight? Also, is it generally better to focus on the same opponent or split up and take separate fights? I'd appreciate hearing how experienced 2v2 players approach these situations.

Why is the brawlhalla community notica ly saltier than other fighting games? Brawlhalla by far has the most vitriol filled, salty, and genuinely angry fanbase when compared to basically any other fighting game. I was wondering why that is because some things that we do don't really happen in other communities whose games fit the same criteria.

We make names for people who play in a style that we don't like, see "Weapon Hogger", "Passive Player", "(Sig) Spammer" etc. . Also interesting is that the game isn't really THAT unbalanced compared to said other fighting games; Street fighter 3rd strike has historically one of the most laughably shitty balancing across characters, imagine if a tournament had 76% lucien players and ulgrim had a ranked winrate of 15%. It is that bad, yet nobody really calls names like "Yun/Chun li abuser".

When it comes to mechanics, those games have their fair share of bullshit too. Street fighter 6 had its throw loops (in short: when you put your opponent in a place where it makes sense to only block, after which you're able to constantly throw them) but nobody called people out individually and instead focused on getting the game changed to fix the issue.
